scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning:
The scenario involves a stepbrother who was allowed to use the Nintendo Switch during a period of babysitting, with a separate profile created to protect the user's own saves. After the babysitting period ended, the user deleted the stepbrother's profile due to personal annoyance with the extra steps required to access their own profile and the eShop. Later, during a Thanksgiving visit, the stepbrother discovered the deletion and became upset, leading to conflict with the father.

Key moral considerations:
- The stepbrother was given access and enjoyed the games, particularly Zelda.
- The deletion was not malicious in intent but was done for convenience, without considering the impact on the stepbrother.
- The stepbrother's emotional reaction indicates he valued the saves and the experience.
- The user acknowledges they usually do not bring the Switch over, suggesting the stepbrother's use was temporary and not intended to be ongoing.
- However, deleting the profile erased the stepbrother's progress, which could be seen as a violation of trust or consideration, especially since the profile was created for him and he was led to believe it was his to use.

The action is morally questionable because:
- It prioritized minor personal convenience over the stepbrother's enjoyment and emotional investment.
- It failed to communicate or consider the stepbrother's feelings, leading to unnecessary distress.
- While the Switch is the user's property and they have the right to manage it, the manner of deletion—without warning or regard for the stepbrother's attachment—lacks empathy and fairness.

Thus, the action is morally unacceptable.
